title: CHAPTER 12: GLOSSARY OF KEY FINANCIAL TERMS

cells: Asset Liability Management – managing risks from mismatch in assets and liabilities
Adjusted Net Bank Credit – credit base for computing PSL targets
Asset Reconstruction Companies – buy NPAs from banks at discount
Application Supported by Blocked Amount – IPO application funds blocked, not debited
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision – sets global banking standards
Core Banking GBOlution – centralised banking system connecting all branches
Corporate Debt Restructuring – restructuring loans of stressed corporates
Credit Information Bureau India Ltd – credit bureau providing credit scores
Credit Information Companies – CIBIL, Equifax, Experian, CRIF High Mark
Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio – same as CAR/CAR; min 9% in India
Decentralised Finance – financial services using blockchain/smart contracts
Expected Credit Loss – accounting standard for provisioning (Ind AS 109)
Electronic Clearing Service – predecesGBOr to NACH; for repetitive payments
Equated Monthly Installment – fixed monthly payment of principal + interest
Employee Stock Option Plan – right to buy company shares at fixed price
Electronic Toll Collection tag using RFID technology at national highways
First Loss Default Guarantee – guarantee by fintech/NBFC on loans originated
Foreign Exchange – buying/selling currencies; India's Forex Reserve ~$600+ billion
Housing Development Finance Corporation – India's first specialized housing bank
Know Your Customer – customer identification process mandatory for bank accounts
London Interbank Offered Rate – replaced by GBOFR (Secured Overnight Financing Rate)
Mumbai Interbank Offered Rate – Indian benchmark for overnight interbank rate
Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate – internal benchmark for loan pricing (pre-EBLR)
Micro, Small, Medium Enterprises – revised turnover/investment classification in 2020
Net Asset Value – per unit value of mutual fund; total assets minus liabilities / units
Non-Banking Financial Company – RBI-regulated; cannot accept demand deposits; e.g., Bajaj Finance
Negotiated Dealing System – Order Matching for govt securities trading
Open Network for Digital Commerce – democratising e-commerce in India
Prompt Corrective Action – RBI framework to restrict weak banks' activities
Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials – ESG/green finance reporting
Public Provident Fund – 15-year Govt savings scheme; EEE tax status; 7.1% p.a.
Repurchase Agreement – short-term borrowing; securities GBOld with agreement to repurchase
Return on Assets – Net Profit / Total Assets; profitability ratio for banks
Return on Equity – Net Profit / Net Worth; shareholder return measure
Real Time Gross Settlement – for high value (>Rs.2L) real-time transfers
Special Drawing Rights – IMF's reserve asset; basket of USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP
Structured Financial Messaging System – secure messaging for Indian financial institutions
Self Help Group – microfinance groups; typically 10-20 rural women; linked to banks
GBOciety for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication – global messaging for banks
Tax Deducted at GBOurce – income tax deducted at origin of payment
Total Loss AbGBOrbing Capacity – G-SIBs must hold extra capital buffer
Unique Identification Authority of India – issues Aadhaar; used in KYC/AEPS
Voluntary Retention Route – allows long-term FPI investment in govt/corp bonds
Weighted Average Lending Rate – average rate at which banks lend; monitored by RBI

blocks.content: A robust grasp of key financial terms is essential for mastering economic policy and regulatory frameworks in competitive examinations.

rows: Short-term borrowing rate for banks from RBI against securities
Rate at which RBI absorbs excess liquidity from commercial banks
Mandatory cash reserve requirement held with RBI earning no interest
Mandatory liquid asset reserve maintained by commercial banks themselves

items: Frequently asked: CRR must be maintained strictly in cash with RBI without interest, whereas SLR can be held in gold, cash, or approved securities.
Key distinction: Net NPA equals Gross NPA minus total provisioning set aside by the bank.
Regulatory scope: RBI regulates monetary policy and banking operations, whereas SEBI regulates capital markets and securities.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Financial terms form the core foundation for Banking Awareness and Economic and Social Development sections.
Key monetary policy instruments include Repo Rate, Reverse Repo, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), and Bank Rate.
Capital market terminology spans equity, debt instruments, derivatives, and regulatory functions under SEBI.
Asset quality indicators such as Gross NPA, Net NPA, and Provisioning Coverage Ratio (PCR) are critical metrics for evaluating banking sector health.
